Network edges and nodes

Source: R/layers-network.R
geom_edge_3d.Rd

geom_edge_3d() draws one edge per row from (x, y, z) to (xend, yend, zend), as a straight line, a circular arc or a shaded tube. geom_node_3d() draws nodes as points. Both map the position columns of a node or edge table by default, so after ggplot(graph) (see fortify.igraph()) they need no mapping; geom_edge_3d() reads the edge table with get_edges_3d().

Usage

geom_edge_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = get_edges_3d(),
  stat = "identity",
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  shape = "line",
  curvature = NULL,
  n = 32L,
  radius = 0.01,
  sides = 12L,
  shade = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

geom_node_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = "identity",
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, stat, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments. The default mapping of geom_edge_3d() is aes(x, y, z = z, xend = xend, yend = yend, zend = zend) and that of geom_node_3d() is aes(x, y, z = z); a supplied mapping overrides these aesthetic by aesthetic.

shape

"line", "arc" or "tube".

curvature

Arc curvature; defaults to 0.5 for arcs and 0 (straight) for tubes. Ignored for lines.

n

Number of points along a curved edge.

radius

Tube radius as a fraction of the longest side of the panel box, for linewidth 0.5; the radius scales with linewidth.

sides

Number of corners of the tube cross-section.

shade

Whether to light faces; defaults to TRUE for tubes.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

Arcs and tubes are built in the model box, after the panel aspect is applied, so they keep their shape for any coord_3d(aspect = ). An arc bends in the plane spanned by the edge and the horizontal direction perpendicular to it; its sagitta is curvature times half the edge length, so curvature = 1 is a half circle and negative values bend the other way, as in ggplot2::geom_curve(). Tubes follow the straight edge, or the arc when curvature is set; their cross-section is a regular polygon with sides corners, carried along the edge with rotation-minimising frames, and they are closed at both ends. The tube colour is the edge colour.

References

Bishop (1975). There is more than one way to frame a curve. American Mathematical Monthly 82, 246-251. doi:10.2307/2319846

See also

fortify.igraph(), stat_layers_3d()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(2)
  g <- igraph::sample_pa(40, directed = FALSE)
  ggplot2::ggplot(g, layout = igraph::layout_with_fr(g, dim = 3)) +
    geom_edge_3d() + geom_node_3d(colour = "steelblue", size = 2) + coord_3d()
  ggplot2::ggplot(g) +
    geom_edge_3d(shape = "tube", colour = "grey60") +
    geom_node_3d(ggplot2::aes(colour = igraph::degree(g)), size = 2) + coord_3d()
}
d <- data.frame(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, xend = 1, yend = 1, zend = 1)
ggplot2::ggplot(d) + geom_edge_3d(shape = "arc", curvature = 0.8) + coord_3d()
